steps.label: dig
steps.sub: what does DNS actually say this name maps to?

code:
$ ping checkout.northbridgeretail.com

PING checkout.northbridgeretail.com (203.0.113.42): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 203.0.113.42: icmp_seq=0 ttl=54 time=11.2 ms
64 bytes from 203.0.113.42: icmp_seq=1 ttl=54 time=10.8 ms
64 bytes from 203.0.113.42: icmp_seq=2 ttl=54 time=12.1 ms

--- checkout.northbridgeretail.com ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 3 received, 0% packet loss
caption: A clean ping proves basic reachability -- it says nothing about the application itself.
Each hop is a router along the path; a stall or timeout here points to where the route breaks down.

code:
$ dig checkout.northbridgeretail.com

;; ANSWER SECTION:
checkout.northbridgeretail.com. 60   IN CNAME northbridgeretail.com.
northbridgeretail.com.          3600 IN A     203.0.113.42

;; Query time: 23 msec
caption: dig shows the exact record, value, and TTL DNS returned -- no browser caching involved.

subtitle: Moving one layer up: checking the application itself, and what's listening locally.
